framing_issues.text: blacked out in the public copy, which doesn't say why
framing_issues.issue: Uneven caveat between sides: 'doesn't say why' is attached only to Georgia Power's redactions (lines 35, 158, 180, 196). PIA Staff's blacked-out estimates (P-147, P-150; lines 190, 271, 307, 319), GAM's (P-112, P-114; lines 295, 331) and GIPL's (P-107; line 152) get no such note, so it can read as a hint that Georgia Power is hiding something.

framing_issues.text: GAM, a manufacturers' group, argues against a bigger credit.
framing_issues.issue: Unequal verbs and an overstated position: GAM is the only party cast as 'arguing against' while others 'back' plans. P-115 'would note' upward pressure on base rates and P-111 says either take-or-pay option would adequately address the concerns if a change is needed. Repeated at lines 162 and 166.

framing_issues.text: Jonathan Ly, GAM's witness, who argues against a bigger credit
framing_issues.issue: Values guide is uneven: the other three lines name the plan the speaker backs ('which backs Plan B/C/D'); this one names none and is tied to Plan A only by the note on line 166.

framing_issues.text: Customers on standard rates get a bigger fuel credit
framing_issues.issue: Reads as a credit on their bills; the glossary (line 120) says the fuel credit is an accounting entry, not a bill credit. Same wording at lines 188 and 196.

framing_issues.text: Homes come out behind in dollars only if nearly all of it does.
framing_issues.issue: States a conditional result as fact: it holds only if the later base-side change is shared by today's class shares (P-116) with no carrying cost, while P-105 says the effect depends on cost allocation. 'it' is also vague. The sentence before it ('that ranking holds however much...') rests on the same unstated assumption.

framing_issues.text: your fuel charge would likely drop, but base rates could later rise to recover the same money
framing_issues.issue: Read alone on the home page: 'drop' is relative to what the charge would otherwise be (timing is 'as determined by the Commission', P-016), and 'the same money' can be read as the same dollars the home saved, though homes pay a larger share of base (58%) than of fuel (55%) revenues (P-116). Same wording on line 15.

framing_issues.text: This case sets how Georgia Power counts some payments
framing_issues.issue: Shown alone on the home page, 'This case' has no referent.

framing_issues.text: Each plan would raise the fuel credit.
framing_issues.issue: 'Each plan' is ambiguous because the page labels today's method 'Plan A', which would not raise the credit.

framing_issues.text: based on its recent storm-cost and fuel-rate changes
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference: 'its' can be read as the home's; P-141 means Georgia Power's approved rate adjustments.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power says it helps pay fixed costs such as pipeline fees, GAM says it can, and GIPL agrees with the idea but says it
framing_issues.issue: Three uses of 'it' with different referents (base-side money, then the idea).

framing_issues.text: because of its later data responses
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference: 'its' can be read as GIPL's; P-155 says the Company's data responses.

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff says Georgia Power could have absorbed its plan
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference: 'its plan' means PIA Staff's plan but can be read as Georgia Power's. Same at line 145.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power's rebuttal says this money "is reducing other costs recovered through base rates
framing_issues.issue: A Georgia Power statement that backs GAM's side sits under GAM's 'What challenges it', contrary to the page's rule (line 221) that the card's own side answers challenges.
Stated as fact here but attributed to Georgia Power at lines 30 and 118 (source is Georgia Power testimony, P-054).

framing_issues.text: GIPL reports concerns that the method raised other customers' fuel costs, "in apparent contravention of Georgia Power
framing_issues.issue: Placed right after Georgia Power's $102 estimate without the caveat line 304 gives (a report of concerns parties raised, not a PSC finding); the pairing invites readers to treat it as a rebuttal.

framing_issues.text: one of three committees on which the commissioners serve
framing_issues.issue: P-023 and P-024 list a 'Facilities Protection' committee as well, so 'three' may be out of date.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Interfaith Power & Light (GIPL), a group of congregations
framing_issues.issue: P-093 describes GIPL and 'its member congregations'; GIPL is an interfaith organization with member congregations, so 'a group of congregations' is a loose gloss (also lines 110 and 158).
Title states the date as certain; the decision is scheduled (P-013) and the order allows until Dec 31 (P-016). 'Decided by Dec 15' on line 29 has the same issue.

framing_issues.text: carrying costs on fuel balances, a discount for income-qualified customers, and gas hedging gains and losses
framing_issues.issue: Technical terms left unexplained for a new reader: 'carrying costs' and 'hedging gains and losses' (also lines 307, 316); 'demand response' (line 245) and 'baseload or intermediate generation' (line 268) appear inside quotes with no gloss.
